title: Confusion of Tongues and Dispersion from Babel
summary: God confounds the language of all the earth and scatters them abroad from Babel (Gen 11:5–9). CFAH dates the Dispersion to 2192/2191 BC.
description: CFAH-2: twelve precise durations (e.g. Aemilius Sura, 1,995 years from Ninus to the defeat of Philip and Antiochus; Eratosthenes, 1,008 years from Menes to the Fall of Troy) converge on 2191 BC for the founding of Assyria and the Egyptian monarchy; CFAH-6 calls it "Anchor Point #2". CFAH-6 notes it falls 157 years after the 2348 BC Flood.

chronologies.citation: Griffith & White, "Chronological Framework of Ancient History. 2: Founding of the Nations," ARJ 15 (2022): 405–426, section "The Dispersion: 2192/2191 BC" and Table 2; Griffith & White, "Chronological Framework of Ancient History. 6: The Old and Middle Kingdoms of Egypt," ARJ 18 (2025): 13–60, Argument 3, "The Dispersion—Anchor Point #2"
chronologies.note: Also CFAH-1 Introduction: "place the Dispersion in 2192/2191 BC".
Not stated in the Jones sources read (Chart No. 1; Chronology of the Old Testament 15th ed. 2002, Chronological Compendium p. 1). Leave empty until verified.

chronologies.date: After the tower-building; no year stated

chronologies.note: Ussher narrates the confusion and dispersion within §47 (heading 1757 AM, 2247 BC) but argues the 13 sons of Joktan "could not be capable of such an expedition ... until some years after Reu was born" (Reu: 1787 AM, 2217 BC, §50). No year given.

chronologies.date: "For aesthetic reasons I shall arbitrarily put the division of the nations in am 1871" ("1871? - Tower of Babel")
chronologies.citation: Jordan, "The Chronology of the Pentateuch (Part 2)," Biblical Chronology 6:4 (April 1994), §7 "The Date of the Tower of Babel" and §8 year list

chronologies.date: Tower of Babel (?): Anno Mundi 1871; 2059 B.C. (SBC)
chronologies.citation: Jordan, "Egypt in Biblical History," Biblical Chronology 5:8 (December 1993), second chart in section "The Beginnings of Egypt"
chronologies.note: Question mark is Jordan's. B.C. year is Jordan's "SBC" (strictest Biblical chronology), which takes Daniel's 70 weeks literally from Cyrus (456 B.C. instead of the conventional 536 B.C.); not comparable one-to-one with Ussher/CFAH B.C. years.

chronologies.citation: Anno Mundi Chronology Studies (unnamed compiler; a compilation of James B. Jordan's system), p. 2, chart "Genesis 11:10 – 12 Genealogy"
chronologies.note: The compiler's own guess: "The Tower of Babel occurred sometime in Peleg’s life. I’m guessing it was before he had Reu, because of Gen.10:25." Jordan himself dates the Tower/Dispersion to AM 1871 (BC 6:4 §7; BC 5:8). Differs from Jordan's own published figure(s): AM 1871, 1871.

chronologies.citation: Preparing the World for Jesus (2nd ed., 2024), ch. 5 "The Babel Rebellion", PDF p. 99 (printed p. 85)
chronologies.note: Dispersion from Babel; heading of ch. V "(2254–2191 BC)"; also pp. 157, 160. Differs from the sort year (2192 BC, cfah-anchor) by 1 years.

chronologies.date: the division of the earth must be placed A. M. 1757, about one hundred and one years after the Flood, when Peleg the son of Eber was born
chronologies.citation: Shuckford, The Sacred and Profane History of the World Connected, 5th ed., revised by James Creighton (London: William Baynes, 1819), vol. 1, Book II, p. 94 (facsimile PDF p. 188)
chronologies.note: He says “if we suppose them to spend nineteen or twenty years in settling and building” before the confusion. Those nineteen or twenty years are not turned into a second Anno Mundi.

chronologies.date: Nimrod’s kingdom and Confusion of Tongues 2554
chronologies.citation: Hales, A New Analysis of Chronology and Geography, History and Prophecy, 2nd ed., corrected and improved (London: C. J. G. & F. Rivington, 1830), vol. II, Synopsis of the Chronology, p. xxxiii
chronologies.note: A different year from “Division of the Earth” 2614 and from Table XI “Dispersion of mankind” 2614.
